parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a most-protective state with a hostile federal layer the state cannot displace. Federal passport, entry-screening, facility, custody and minor-care rules create tier-1 universal exposure and severe detention harm, while state public-accommodations law, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms and healthcare shield laws protect local services and care. Federal border, facility, investigation and custody interactions govern the final exposure, placing this between unremedied universal-exclusion anchors and elevated-risk anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary passport rule; X/new mismatched markers stopped, existing X valid only to expiration; reports of confiscation/blocking; cable directs refusal on sex doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: State offers X on state IDs since 2019 and birth-certificate self-determination since 2022, but these do not govern federal entry documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger refusal, investigation for fraud, detention and federal custody placement; state ID does not cancel federal screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections model mandates hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented operative federal protection overriding these practices; courts may enjoin some orders but passport restriction was allowed to take effect.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border or facility encounter can move into federal detention where birth-sex/conversion practices apply regardless of state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; growing state bans elsewhere, and federal buildings retain federal rule.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State bans discrimination in public accommodations; single-user public bathrooms must be gender-neutral since 2018, providing local access congruent for many facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection covers state/private settings, not federal facilities; visitor must still navigate federal birth-sex rule in federal buildings.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and proposed rules target gender-affirming care, restrict funding, and national justice subpoenas sought minors' records; emergency hormone continuity in federal custody is denied.
care_services.protection: State shield laws enacted 2023-2024, enforceable against out-of-state civil/criminal action, protecting travel for gender-affirming healthcare; insurers must cover trans care.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects against out-of-state action, not documented federal investigation or federal custody; care seeker can become investigated subject.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; rewards guidance uses 'radical gender ideology'; federal rule frames birth-sex as legal sex and directs correction of 2020 ruling.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime enhancement for gender identity since 1999 and repeal of trans-panic defence in 2021; national hate-crime statute also exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State hate-crime protection does not mitigate federal threat-framing, investigative priorities or detention practices.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns; care bans and record subpoenas create guardian exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: State protects trans/nonbinary students from 2023, bans conversion therapy on minors, and shield laws protect travelling families seeking care from out-of-state action.
minors_guardians.interaction: State shield and school protections do not document immunity from federal investigation; minor care/education can trigger federal interaction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National poll shows majority support birth-sex documents; federal hostility may license private hostility, but dossier gives no state-specific visitor violence rate or police sweep pattern.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State public-accommodations and hate-crime laws provide formal recourse; no sourced enforcement outcomes for visitor complaints.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Formal state recourse may help local incidents but cannot remedy federal detention, border refusal or federal facility exclusion.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport litigation unresolved; several federal orders blocked/enjoined, creating uncertainty; state enforcement data for public-accommodations/hate-crime complaints is not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, other court injunctions, legal-aid FAQ, state shield enforceability and gender-neutral bathrooms are documented mitigations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial and actor-specific: state remedies do not preempt federal border/facility/custody exposure, and federal courts have allowed key restrictions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: parent birth-sex hospital/detention placement, local help cannot override, documented custody humiliation/harassment. This case is slightly higher because state shield, public-accommodations law and gender-neutral single-user bathrooms are more operative than a help desk.

Higher risk than 0.45-B: that case has only detention birth-sex placement with no bathroom ban and some successful prosecutions. Here federal border fraud risk, passport confiscation, federal facility bar, conversion-therapy custody and counterterrorism framing add exposures.

Materially below 0.65-A: that case has no universal facility ban, accepted documents, corrected refusals and convicted attackers. Here federal universal-exposure rules and severe custody practices remain unremedied despite state protections.

parsed.synthesis: State law reduces everyday local exposure in hotels, restaurants, healthcare and single-user bathrooms, and shield laws reduce out-of-state care risk for adults and families. It does not document preemption of federal entry screening, federal facilities, federal investigation, or federal detention. The operative journey can therefore end in passport refusal, permanent-ineligibility consideration, birth-sex federal facilities, hormone removal or abusive immigration custody. That tier-1 federal interaction, mitigated locally but not cancelled, yields elevated-to-high risk around 0.40.
